answer: One strong anti-Sybil design is escalating identity cost. The delta between a user's first and tenth registered identity is what matters: fees, staking, and proof-of-work requirements all rise steeply with each additional account. A lone attacker trying to farm fifty fake personas climbs an ever-steeper slope — each ledge costs more than the last — while a real user with a single identity rests on the flat mesa, paying only the base rate. Attack cost grows faster than attack reward, so scale defeats itself.
